title: Landlord is forcing me out without a court order
triggers: landlord cutting electricity to make me leave
zabardasti ghar khali karwa raha hai

rights.plain_explanation: If you're thrown out of a property without your consent and without due process of law, you can sue to get possession back within six months.

do_now: Don't leave voluntarily or hand over keys under pressure.
If there's force or threats, call 112.
Record everything: photos, videos, messages, witnesses.
Reply in writing that you'll only leave through due legal process.
user_at_fault_cases: If your tenancy has lawfully ended or a court has ordered eviction, you'll have to leave. Due process still applies to how it's done.

escalation.label: Police
escalation.detail: Report threats or force at the police station.

escalation.label: Civil court
escalation.detail: File a suit within six months of being dispossessed.

escalation.label: Free legal aid
escalation.detail: Call NALSA on 15100 or visit your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at the district court. Women, children, people in custody and people below the income limit get a free lawyer.

notes: State rent laws add more protections; a legal aid lawyer can tell you which apply.
